problems.source_says: The Methods describe an experiment involving 480 human participants, and the abstract says those participants wrote emails. The following page restricts the sample to responses passing an attention check and taking more than 15 minutes, without giving the number retained or explicitly linking 480 to the sample after those filters. No analyzed participant total appears in the available results or figure captions. The form explicitly substitutes the reported study sample for an analyzed count; that substitution is not independently confirmed. The verified post-filter n_analyzed is unknown and should be null pending the supplementary methods/tables or data; this is an unsupported count, not evidence that the true count differs from 480.
problems.quote: The sample includes all responses that passed the attention check and in which participants took more than the 15-minute suggested time.
problems.locator: PDF p. 1, abstract; p. 2, Methods, Study 2; p. 3, Methods continuation, sample-inclusion sentence; pp. 3-8, results and Figs. 1-3. SI Section A, Fig. S1 and Tables S3-S5 are referenced but absent from the saved PDF.

problems.source_says: The overview reports 240 people shown AI-generated content. That is explicit evidence of exposure to the treatment, but it does not state how many treated people remained in the analysis after the attention-check and completion-time inclusion rule. The available PDF supplies neither an arm-specific exclusion count nor a final analyzed count; the verified analyzed count for this arm is unknown and should be null.

confirmed.statement: Study 1 concerns 600 AI-generated responses to 200 prompts across three languages, rated by six evaluators, two per language; those are not 600 human experimental participants.
Six evaluators rated Study 2 emails; their ratings are not additional randomized writers. The PDF does not identify whether these evaluators also rated Study 1.

confirmed.statement: The stated inclusion rule requires passing the attention check and taking more than the suggested 15 minutes. Separate pre-filter recruitment/randomization totals and excluded or retained counts by arm are not reported in the available article.

summary: The paper reports 480 participants, with 240 per arm, but does not explicitly establish these as the counts remaining after its attention-check and completion-time filters. The analyzed counts and the minimum of 50 analyzed people remain unconfirmed because the supplementary materials and linked data could not be accessed.
